και ὁπε[ ] γραμμα̣[ μ]ε νου τ̣η[ ἐ]κκλησ̣[ια· ]ος μοι̣· δι̣ω̣κ̣το̣[υ γαρ το]υτο· οὐτε τοις
εὐσ[εβεσι]ν ἐπεσκηψα· εὐη̣[θες γα]ρ και ἀνο̣ητον· [τους δε] διαταρ̣[α]τ̣τοντα̣[ς τη(ν)]
παρ' ἡμ̣ι̣ν ἐκκλη̣[σια(ν)] και τον [κ]ατ' αὐτη[ν φι][λο]χ̣ριστο̣ν̣ λαον α[···]υ
thought_title: Rejection of imposed commands and condemnation of church disturbers
orientation: Cyril continues his defense, denying that he imposed anything on the pious and condemning those who disturb the church and its Christ-loving people.
pass_a_gloss: and the [text broken] letter of the [text broken] church [text broken] to me; for this is [text broken] of a persecutor; neither did I impose upon the pious; for it is foolish and senseless; but those who disturb the church among us and the Christ-loving people in it [text broken]

choices.why: The verb ἐπισκήπτω here means to enjoin or impose a command upon someone; the dative εὐσεβεσιν marks the recipients.

choices.english: for it is foolish and senseless
choices.why: The two adjectives describe the alleged imposition as both simple-minded and lacking sense; the glossary does not cover these, so plain literal renderings are used.
The participle with article functions as a substantive: those who disturb; the prefix δια- intensifies the disturbance.
The compound adjective φιλόχριστος means loving Christ; it modifies λαόν, the people of the church.

pass_b_english: And the letter . . . to me from the church . . . For this is the act of a persecutor. [The papyrus is broken here; the letter's sender and content are unknown.] Nor did I impose anything upon the pious, for that would be foolish and senseless. But those who disturb the church among us and its Christ-loving people . . .
notes: The source text is heavily damaged with many lacunae and uncertain letters. The gloss reflects only what is legible; no text has been invented.
The phrase 'διωκτου γαρ τουτο' is partially restored; the reading 'of a persecutor' is tentative.
The final word after λαον is broken and unreadable.

problems.fix: For this is the act of a persecutor

last_rejected.quote: For this is the act of a persecutor
last_rejected.why: διωκτου is genitive singular, 'of a persecutor,' but τουτο is neuter singular 'this.' The phrase means 'for this [belongs to/is characteristic of] a persecutor,' not 'the act of a persecutor.' The English adds 'act' which is not in the source and changes the sense from a characteristic to a specific deed.
last_rejected.fix: For this is the mark of a persecutor.
last_rejected.ruling: διωκτου γαρ τουτο: supplying 'act/deed' for elliptical genitive is standard; meaning 'this is characteristic of a persecutor' is preserved.

last_rejected.why: The glossary does not cover these terms, but 'foolish' for εὐηθες is inaccurate: εὐήθης means simple-minded, naive, silly in a gentle sense, while ἀνόητον means senseless, unintelligent. 'Foolish' conflates two distinct Greek words with different tones; εὐήθης is more 'simple-minded' or 'naive.'
last_rejected.ruling: εὐηθες and ἀνοητον: 'foolish and senseless' renders both within normal range; distinction between naive and unintelligent is nuance, not error.
